trust_decision.summary: outfile_write() trusts that username + hash + plain (from the hash-list line, up to HCBUFSIZ_LARGE each) fit into the fixed HCBUFSIZ_LARGE tmp_buf, and appends each field with unbounded memcpy/hex_encode/exec_hexify and index writes.

landing_point.why: Summary names outfile_write() and the username; the plain-format username memcpy is the first copy in that function.

fix_sites.module_kind: output formatter, JSON branch (hex_encode of username/hash/plain, 2x expansion)
output formatter, plain branch, username field
output formatter, numeric fields via snprintf with stale length arithmetic

fix_sites.entry_point: CLI crack output with --outfile-autohex / hexplain format
fix_sites.module_kind: output formatter, $HEX[] and hexplain plain fields

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All published changes are inside one function, src/outfile.c:528-740 (fix.diff:5-316).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For potfile_write_append (src/potfile.c:253-303): it has no username field, and its hash comes from an encoder already bounded to HCBUFSIZ_LARGE, so a solver would say the 'oversized username' report does not apply to the potfile writer.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An oversized entry must still be written, truncated, not dropped (fix comment). Long legitimate hashes and usernames in --show/--left output, $HEX[] autohex output and the trailing separator layout must keep working. A fix that rejects long hash lines, skips the entry or caps the username to a small length breaks this.

O6_input_shapes: raw username copied in plain format (src/outfile.c:609)
hex-encoded username in JSON format, 2x expansion (src/outfile.c:550)
raw hash field (src/outfile.c:665) and hex-encoded hash in JSON (src/outfile.c:578)
single-byte separator/brace/quote writes past the end (src/outfile.c:615, src/outfile.c:597)
snprintf numeric fields whose length arithmetic goes stale or negative once tmp_len passes the buffer (src/outfile.c:628, src/outfile.c:653, src/outfile.c:736)

O7_producer.where: The username comes from the hash-list loader, which takes it from the input line through hlfmt_user and hcstrdup with no length cap (src/hashes.c:1767-1801). The input line can be up to HCBUFSIZ_LARGE. This is a parser and fits none of the listed producer kinds.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: potfile_write_append builds hash + separator + $HEX[plain] in the same HCBUFSIZ_LARGE potfile tmp_buf with unbounded memcpy/exec_hexify and index writes; the fix leaves it untouched.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: There is no username in it, and out_len is already bounded by hash_encode/module_hash_encode_potfile to HCBUFSIZ_LARGE (src/hashes.c:1002-1015). It looks like a separate potfile feature.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different file (src/potfile.c vs src/outfile.c), same package; reached from check_hash at src/hashes.c:1018

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Add the username or dynamic-x field to the potfile append line, in the same unbounded style.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The function already mirrors outfile_write's field-by-field layout, and the show/left paths already carry username and dynamicx next to it (src/potfile.c:706-736).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Emit dynamicx_buf into outfile_write output, with a new appender that skips the bound.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The show/left paths collect dynamicx_buf and never use it. A maintainer adding it to the output would copy the existing memcpy pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Pass the user's username into the live crack output (currently NULL, 0).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A natural feature request (--username in live output) that sends the attacker-sized username through a second caller and buffer (hashes->tmp_buf, src/hashes.c:3012).

O9_family: memory safety: heap buffer overflow from unbounded composition of variable-length fields into a fixed buffer (CWE-120)

O10_build.project_tests: There is no unit test for outfile_write. tools/test.sh and tools/test_edge.sh are end-to-end cracking scripts that need a backend. --show/--left skip backend init (src/backend.c:5552-5553), so the username route runs on CPU without a device.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Clamp user_len before the username memcpy at src/outfile.c:609 and leave the hash, $HEX/hexplain, JSON hex_encode and single-byte writes unbounded.

out_of_scope_notes: out_buf[out_len] = 0 after encoders given the full HCBUFSIZ_LARGE capacity can write one byte past the end if an encoder fills it (src/potfile.c:697-704, src/hashes.c:1015).
For split hashes, the second hash_encode writes at out_buf + 16 and out_len is summed (src/potfile.c:699-701).
unverified: Whether any hash mode's encoder can produce an out_len within ~520 bytes of HCBUFSIZ_LARGE (16 MiB). If none can, the potfile_write_append route cannot be triggered by behavioural tests. That is why pattern_fit is injection_only, not B.
Repo size in MB was not measured (no shell). hashcat with its OpenCL kernels and modules is likely 100-300 MB, so neither tiny_repo nor giant_repo.
present_in_latest is unknown because no latest release was provided.

Effectively a single function: all 6 fix sites sit in outfile_write. single_site is not set because the definition needs one place, and an unverified O8 route exists. Treat this as a near-single_site host (lessons: single-location fixes never made a task hard).
